description: ProdigeUI Quality Gate criteria. Every design output is evaluated against these. Overall passes only when ALL criteria pass.

criteria.description: Repeated visual roles are declared at a token-definition boundary and consumed through semantic variables. Raw literals are allowed inside token definitions and one-off generated artwork, but not as repeated component styling.
Normal text contrast ratio >= 4.5:1
Large text and non-text UI contrast >= 3:1
All interactive elements have visible focus indicator (3:1 contrast)
All interactive elements fully operable via keyboard
All spacing values from token scale (multiples of 4px)

Font sizes follow a coherent scale — a modular ratio (e.g. 1.25) for UI text, OR a fluid clamp() display ramp for expressive headlines. Arbitrary unrelated sizes fail; systematic fluid display type does not.
Maximum 2 typefaces + monospace
Display, body, and optional annotation typography have declared, distinct, repeated jobs appropriate to the product; font switching is functional rather than decorative.
Custom fonts are loaded before visual evaluation and the computed family on display text matches the declared display face; silent fallback is a failure.
The closing CTA reuses an established semantic signal/accent or primary surface, owns its foreground, and does not introduce a new or muddy near-match hue.

Expressive portfolio, studio, editorial, fashion, and creative-marketing galleries use at least two independent asymmetry signals: dominance plus offset, stagger, crop or height variation, overlap, or intentional negative space. Repeated proportional grids and consecutive reuse of the same container topology fail.
Project title, category, year, and primary identity cue remain visible without hover or focus. Touch, reduced-motion, screenshot, and static-preview states must not erase project meaning.
Rendered project geometry preserves declared dominance, span, crop, and height variation. A shared fixed height, aspect ratio, or min-height that visually equalizes intended unequal items fails.

Expressive pages resolve with proposition-scale type, one specific action, useful contact/navigation/availability context, and continuity with an earlier motif. A thin copyright or social row alone fails.

The closing chapter uses no more than one ambient visual system behind one proposition, one primary action, and one compact context row. When the brief explicitly requires closing footage, the video must remain that ambient system with a poster, responsive crop, reduced-motion fallback, and readable scrim. Dropping it for a flat footer, duplicate marquees, repeated slogans, or competing video/particle systems fails.
Every CSS or Tailwind utility that expects a scalar color resolves to a scalar color value. Gradient objects, shadow objects, and composite theme namespaces interpolated into scalar utilities fail.

Every safe supplied URL, explicitly requested dependency, named section or content job, named interaction, and literal content item has concrete source evidence. Security, accessibility, reduced-motion, and collision safety may replace an unsafe technique, but the requested visible intent must remain. Silent flattening into generic static sections fails.

When a canonical accepted quality profile applies, the output transfers its semantic product intent, artifact credibility, type roles, palette commitment, focal hierarchy, rhythm, and closing behavior without copying benchmark copy or geometry.
Maximum four perceptual font-weight bands. Nearby variable-font values that resolve to the same 100-weight band count as one role.
Layout follows 12/8/4 column grid system
All interactive components document all applicable states
Components render using active theme tokens only
All motion respects prefers-reduced-motion

Discrete UI transitions (hover, state change, entrance, modal) do not exceed ~1000ms. Continuous/ambient/looping decorative motion (marquee, background video loop, scroll-linked parallax, grain) is EXEMPT — it is continuous, not a discrete transition.
Clear size/weight differentiation between heading levels
Navigation has <= 7 items per level
Interactive elements >= 44px on mobile, >= 32px on desktop
No AI-slop patterns in their SLOP form. FLAG techniques (glass, parallax, gradients, big type, decorative motion) pass in their CRAFT form per anti-ai-slop.checklist.md discriminators.

For expressive use-cases (DESIGN_VARIANCE >= 0.6 or MOTION_INTENSITY >= 0.5): output demonstrates craft — a hero signature technique, choreographed motion, texture/depth, distinctive display typography, real media, and a clear focal point. Passing the negative slop gate alone is NOT sufficient. See quality-gate/positive-patterns.md and craft/.

Expressive hero is anchored by a REAL focal subject (video, photo, product/UI, 3D render, or deliberate oversized display type). A blurry CSS gradient/mesh as the hero subject FAILS (the NOVA regression). Gradient may be textural behind real media/type, never the empty subject. See craft/compositions/.
No gray placeholder boxes, div-based fake screenshots, or 'image here' stand-ins on expressive work. Real media required where the brief implies it. See assets/asset-sourcing.guide.md.
Hero-scale display type uses a deliberate display face (reflex-reject procedure in craft/taste.md) with negative tracking and tight leading — not untouched system/Inter at hero scale.

Binary taste checks pass (craft/taste.md): no em-dash in copy; no reflex cream/beige body bg; eyebrow count <= ceil(sections/3); no hover-scale; no default gradient text; no hero-metric template; outcome-specific CTA copy; two-altitude slop test passes.

Decorative glow/radial elements must dissolve into atmosphere (never visible as a distinct geometric shape). Constraints: gradient inner rgba alpha <= 0.16; size <= 50vw or 560px; filter:blur >= 20px; gradient terminates to transparent by 70% radius. A glow that reads as a solid circle/ellipse is a FAIL. See effects-catalog.md 'Ambient glow bloom'.

Every element with position:absolute MUST have an explicit positioned ancestor (position:relative on the intended parent). Without this, percentage-based width/height compute against an unintended container, causing elements (e.g. toggle thumbs, slider indicators) to render at viewport-scale size. This is a critical layout bug.

All image containers (img parent or element with background-image) MUST define a background-color fallback (e.g. var(--surface-2)). Without this, failed/blocked images render as broken icons or browser-chosen placeholder shapes instead of a graceful colored rectangle. See assets/fallback-images.md.
Complex interfaces use progressive disclosure (<= 5 decisions/screen)
All components use appropriate ARIA roles
System provides visual feedback within 400ms of user action (Doherty Threshold)
Related elements grouped by proximity (whitespace) not borders/boxes
No more than 4 unchunked items displayed without visual grouping
Generated HTML has valid document semantics and UTF-8 text, produces no runtime errors, and makes no unexpected external requests during deterministic evaluation.
Rendered desktop and mobile viewports have zero horizontal overflow.
Meaningful headings, paragraphs, articles, sections, and main content remain visible in the final rendered state, including reduced-motion mode.
Every rendered image and media dependency loads successfully in the evaluated artifact.
The primary actor, desired outcome, and specific value mechanism are understandable in the first meaningful task or viewport. A category label, visual mood, or generic promise alone fails.

A differentiator is visible through truthful product evidence, workflow, comparison, service pathway, material proof, or decision model. Palette, typography, and decorative geometry alone do not count.

The primary journey has an intelligible path from entry through orientation, evidence, choice, action, feedback, result, and next or recovery behavior. A polished fragment with no credible continuation fails.

Every applicable default, loading, empty, invalid/error, permission/eligibility, success, and returning-context state is designed or explicitly marked N/A with a reason. Errors identify what happened and how to recover.

Information density, terminology, proof, interaction commitment, and trust behavior fit the intended market, user knowledge, decision cost, and regulation. Familiar conventions are preserved where they protect comprehension or safety.

For a materially new domain, the artifact records at least two current, direct market references and extracts the entry pattern, evidence grammar, commitment/risk, convention to preserve, product-specific departure, and rejected generic fallback. It does not copy a reference identity, copy, assets, or geometry.

The selected experience archetype controls the first viewport, information topology, and next action. A generic marketing hero, dashboard, gallery, split panel, or form without a task rationale fails.

The dominant visual or product state actively reduces the user's decision uncertainty. Physical products, place, care, work, and learning contexts use truthful relevant evidence rather than abstract geometry, blank panels, or decorative fake UI.

Relative to an unrelated artifact, at least four of first-viewport topology, type behavior, palette posture, media role, density, action placement, and section sequence change when the user job or market evidence changes. Repainting a shared page shell fails.

The first viewport exposes one primary decision, its truthful proof, and only the safety, cost, eligibility, or context needed now. Decision-time, action-result, exception/recovery, and returning-context information remains reachable and preserves context, but does not become permanent visual furniture without a task or risk reason.
At compact viewports, users can still find the primary evidence, take the primary action, receive feedback, and recover from failure. Passing overflow checks alone is insufficient.

The visible experience has realistic semantic controls, component boundaries, data/asset behavior, focus management, and interaction constraints. Decorative fake UI or impossible state transitions fail.

The persistent header or navigation preserves context required for the current user task. At compact widths, the primary route remains reachable through a deliberate replacement or documented narrower scope; merely hiding generic links fails.

Surface, text, action, selected, focus, success, warning, error, and unavailable colours have task-specific roles with verified foreground/background pairings. A decorative palette with untested state combinations fails.

Every material action has an inspectable idle, pressed, pending, success or changed state, error or recovery route, focus treatment, and risk-proportionate confirmation, undo, or escalation. A label-only button fails.

Repeated and rapidly interrupted interactions retarget cleanly. Drawers, toasts, tabs, and overlays preserve semantic controls, focus, keyboard behavior, reduced-motion completeness, and realistic compact-device constraints.

Material typography, colour, header, action, or motion choices are accompanied by a concrete candidate comparison, product hypothesis, selected treatment, rejected treatment, and rendered test context. Unexamined defaults fail.
